utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is essentially a meeting that the Trial Chamber is having with the expert about the -- appointed as a handwriting expert and for which the parties are invited to attend, and in fact I would like to register the presence in the courtroom of Defence attorneys, Madam Vidovic and Mr. Jones, assisted by their respective case manager and legal assistant. And on the Prosecution's side, Mr. Wubben, assisted by Mr. Di Fazio and their case manager. And particularly I should like to note the presence of the accused himself, Mr. Oric, and I should like to start this meeting precisely by asking Mr. Oric to confirm if he is receiving interpretation of the proceedings in his own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Oric, and good morning to you. And I also wish good morning to everyone present -- present here, particularly the parties. So we have in the courtroom here a gentleman. I understand that your name is Dorijan Kerzan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I understand I can address you in English because you can understand the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: However, to make sure -- we have interpretation in Serbo-Croat. If you have interested in following the proceedings in that language, I think you would need to switch on to channel 6, to channel 6, if you want to follow the proceedings in Serbo-Croat. Now, Mr. Kerzan, we have never met, so what I suggest is that you introduce yourself first and foremost and tell us a few things about yourself. Of course, we have been briefed and I have information -- when I say "I," it's we actually. We have information about you which we have examined, and I also have a -- kind of a CV in front of me with -- which bears a signature under the name of Dr. Dorijan Kerzan. I suppose you have a copy of it. I'm going to show it to you, and you confirm that this is your signature to start with. And then I propose that if the parties are not yet in possession of a copy of this, we'll make you privy to it -- or you have already. But I just want a confirmation from the witness himself that that is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: It is the same as the originals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Mr. Kerzan, you're not really here as a witness yet. Basically this is a kind of an interview and meeting we are having with you to make sure that you know exactly what you -- we require from you and discuss a few items with you before we send you back to beautiful Ljubljana to do the work we are going to ask you to do for us. Yes. Could you tell us who -- who you are, what's your experience in the matter of forensic handwriting examination, very briefly, because then when you return back to give testimony, you are obviously going to be asked by both -- by both parties on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, I started work as a forensic handwriting expert in 1992, 1st of July. It was -- I started then. I was appoint -- I was taken in to the forensic lab as a linguist specialist. I was asked to do linguistic examination of text, but the point was that linguistics -- linguist analysis are very rare in our country, so I had to go to start training for the handwriting training right from the start. From 1997 I'm head of the department of handwriting and document analysis, that means nine years, and from the year 2000 -- July 2000 I was appointed as an expert witness in handwriting by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Slovenia, which I have copies here. If there is any other information besides CV needed, I can provide also, but I think that's mainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is that whatever you have available by a way of explaining your credentials or describing your credentials, the better it would be. I'll ask you one simple question. I suppose I know the answer already, but I wish to put it on record. Do you write and understand Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I did learn -- I don't do that every day, but I did do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you're familiar with the Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the Cyrillic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. One question -- I also want to make sure before we confirm your appointment as our expert that you have not been approached by anyone in relation to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I have been approached by -- only by the Court, only by the colleague that works here; otherwise no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's in these last few days in relation to what we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- and you've -- when did you become aware of the existence of this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you -- you've never watched TV transmissions of the proceedings of this case in your country? If they --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I've just seen something on the news, but not really I've been watching that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We have got a rather limited exercise for you, and what I suggest to do this morning very briefly is the following. I will show you one by one ten documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- each of which bears a signature. It is precisely that signature in each of these ten documents that you need to examine --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- for authenticity purposes. For comparative analysis purposes, we are going to give you what I would call a source document which basically contains eight specimen signatures allegedly by the accused. What you have to do is to compare the signatures which are allegedly of the accused, these eight documents -- eight signature -- specimen signatures that I'm going to be giving you to be used as source signatures, with the signatures in the other ten documents that I mentioned, and then report to us in a way that I will explain later whether any of the signatures in the ten documents match with any of the signatures which I have called specimen signatures or source signatures. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also would like to know if, in your opinion, your expert opinion, there has been any tampering with any of the ten documents to be examined. Then in addition we are going to give you another document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You will receive these terms in writing as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I still want to write it myself. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then in addition we're going to give you another document which also bears a signature, and again you need to compare that signature with the source signatures and report to us whether you can reach any conclusion whether it matches or whether it doesn't match or what your opinion is. But let's go through the documents one by one. And for the record I will be mentioning the ERN number. You will also need to undertake with us that you will not use any -- any -- you -- any analysis which could affect the integrity of the documents, in other words either destroy or alter the present state of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think that is quite clear and you would need to sign a declaration. The first document that we would like you to examine is the one I'm going give you now, and which bears ERN 00926461. Please show it to the expert. All right. It's the signature in the bottom that you would need to examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not tell you what it is. You're the expert, you will then tell us what it is. All right. But that's -- that's what I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And then you come back to us with your conclusions whether it's good enough for analysis or not and what your conclusion is. Now I'm going to give you another document -- for the record also, in order to make sure that the parties can follow, that is P3 in the record. All right? That is P3. I'm going to give you another document now with ERN 01239504, and for your information this is P4. Yes, he keeps these, yes. And then of course he will sign us a receipt. One -- yes. Again, it's that signature in the bottom that you need to examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The next document I'm going to hand to you bears ERN 01239528 and it is P13. All right? Now I'm going to give you another document which is P14 and it bears ERN 01239544.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the next document is P37 and it bears ERN number 01839608. Next document is P73 and it bears ERN number 02075808. And again, in each case, Dr. Kerzan, it's the signature in the bottom in each of these documents that we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: On this particular document I would say the right one or the left one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: There are two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. You're right. Can you hand it back to me to be sure. There are two signatures, one allegedly according to -- on the face of the document because, of course this is, as you can imagine, very much debated here. There is one on the right which -- there is one on the left which says [B/C/S spoken]. We are not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are interested in the signature on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where the stamp is. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next document is -- again bears two signatures. It has ERN 02075809, it's P74. We are only interested in the signature on the right, behind the stamp. And I'm going to give you now P75 which is 02075810. Again, it -- it has two signatures. We are not interested in the signature on the left nor in the handwriting on the text; we are only interested in the signature on the right in the bottom on -- where the stamp is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am now going to give you document with ERN 01239545, which in our records is P158. We are interested in the signature, the bottom right. And finally I'm going to give you another document with ERN 03721400 which is Exhibit P210. Please don't ask me -- it's the signature in the bottom right. Please don't ask me if this is a photocopy or not. That completes the first list, the one of ten documents. Now I am going to give you another document, and I think we can give him only this page. We don't need to give him -- okay. We don't need to give him this because there is no signatures on this. I'm going to give you one page from Exhibit P269. The page I am going to give you if -- I would appreciate, Katarina, if you can provide me with a plastic sheet, if you have one, please. The page I am going to give you bears ERN number 01801583. It contains a signature, bottom right. No, no, did I say 85? No, I said "83." And I'm not going to comment anything on this except that I would like you similarly to examine this signature by comparing it to the documents that I will be giving you very shortly. So we need to put this in a plastic sheet, please. I am returning these to you because they belong. Right. Now I need to find the other one. Yeah, the P100. Doctor, I am now going to give you the following documents. I will go through them one by one. First, for the record, the first page is 02066400. This is part of P100, Ms. Vidovic and Mr. Wubben. This is part of P100 that I am going through now, all right, one by one. The second page is 02066401. The third is 02066402. The fourth is 02066403. The fifth is 02066404. The sixth is 02066405. The seventh is 02066406. And finally the eighth is 02066407. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, on each of these documents there is more than one signature, as you will see. We are only interested in each case in the signature that appears in blue ink - what kind of an ink I don't know, it's a ball-point or whatever, you should be able to establish that - in the top of each of these eight pages. At the top there is a signature in each of these eight pages with a date and a time. For the purpose of your analysis, these are the signatures that you are to use for comparative purposes as source signatures. I wish to make it very clear that you are to ignore completely any other signatures that appear on these documents. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please hand these -- again, I wish if you could provide the expert with a plastic pocket if you have. I mean ... You will understand - I'm sure I don't need to stress this beyond what is minimal - that we need to keep a record of the fact that we are handing you these documents for analysis purposes. So you will now be approached by a member of our staff from the Registry with a list of the documents indicating the ERN number --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- which you are kindly asked to sign. That would be a confirmation on your part that you have received them for analysis purposes. You will also be then required later on to hand them back in the same condition they are without any alterations or markings or whatever to -- the member of the Registry that I am designating and that would be Ms. Fabian, Katarina, that you are seeing in front of you, right in front of you. So -- but these are procedures that we will attend to after this sitting, and you will deal precisely with the Registrar. Have I made myself clear as to what you are required to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I have here material for comparison, and if I understand correctly, one document -- these documents are to be treated together and these separately in comparison purposes or whatever way I do it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you do it whichever way you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm giving it to you separately because on the face of it the writing or the signature in this P269 looks to be different to the eye than the signature in the other ten documents. So I am saying: Keep it apart for -- analyse it in the same way but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- I think I would have misled you by telling you: Have 11 instead of 10 and treat them as if -- so I think I send my message clear. Otherwise, if you have any questions or any problems with the documents that I have given you, perhaps you could tell us now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I need more time to see if there is any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: But it would be unprofessional to say anything at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So your task would be to make this comparative study, to report to us whether in your opinion, whether there has been any tampering of any of those documents. And if there are any other matters that you can highlight to us which could help us establish the authenticity or otherwise of any of those 11 documents, please do so by all means. We would prefer if you can prepare and hand in your findings in writing, and this brings me obviously to the time-frame that you require and what -- what I need to know from you, basically, is how much time you need to do -- to carry out the analysis, how much time you need to prepare the report, have it typed and with the maps and everything, and be communicated to us before you come over to testify -- and I would require an original plus five copies, an original plus five copies. And then you need to tell us roughly when you could be at the disposal of the Trial Chamber for testimony because -- for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, it is, in my view, logical that I would prepare an opinion in writing, of course. Within the opinion I would also explain the methods I would use and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about them now, because that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, concerning the time-frame, I would say three to four weeks I need to prepare an opinion. It wouldn't be wise to do it faster because this method we are using is method approved by ENFSI [Realtime ranscript read in error "embassy"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Approved by embassy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: ENFSI, actually, the Network of Forensic Handwriting Experts, not embassy. So it's very good within this method to have opinion prepared and then leave it aside for a couple of days and think it over to do it again. I always do analysis twice, at least, just to avoid possible mistakes or possible misjudgement. So it takes three to four weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- let's do it this way. I would leave it to you to decide exactly how much time you require, but my recommendation is that we -- we haven't given you much documents. My recommendation is that the moment you are sure of yourself and in a position to file a report, to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We would also need to know from you when you can then come here to testify to confirm your report, first and foremost, and to be asked questions, et cetera. I'm urging you to do this analysis the earliest possible because you will understand that the parties have to be given every opportunity to come back to us -- not only to ask you questions but also to come back to us if need be with further information on -- on these -- on these issues. So if you can change this matter up or give it your utmost attention it would be much better. But since considering what you said, the last thing I'm going to do is impress on you the need to -- to finish before you think you -- you can really present us with a good -- with a good analysis. So I would leave it that for the time being. What I would like you to do is to come back to us when in the course of the next week or two you are in a position more or less to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the earliest we can expect the report, then I can communicate the date of the sitting to you and also -- please, also indicate your availability. I can then indicate the date of the sitting to both parties so that they can make their preparations, if they need to have an expert sitting by their side when you give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I just have a question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: About the written report, do I send it to you or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You send it -- you communicate it -- when you -- when it's ready --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- we can either arrange to have it picked up from you by --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if the Tribunal has a representative in Ljubljana, I doubt it, I doubt it, but we will let you know. It will either be picked up by the member of the Registrar -- of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or else we -- you can send the copies of the Registrar and then bring the original with you when you come to give testimony. We will let you know about the protocol to be used, but the important thing is that we have an indication. If you can file a -- your report in English, it will be better, but we are not forcing you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you think it's better filed in Serbo-Croat, then by all means go in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, I would have -- it is very difficult to prepare an expert opinion in the non-native language because one comma can change the meaning of the words. So I would prefer to do it in my language, which is Slovenian, but I can provide you with a summary in English, or some kind of a shortened report, so to be understood -- the opinion to be understood on spot when you received it. That I would do, but I wouldn't write all the report in English because, as I said, any wrong use of word can mean bad, bad things. So I wouldn't dare to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So -- how different is Slovenian from Serbo-Croat? Because I must confess my ignorance in the -- completely different? Completely different I would imagine?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very different, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But don't worry, I think -- I think we should aim at the optimum in these matters, so the report will be in Slovenian. And, Katarina, in the meantime communicate this matter to the Registrar. I'm sure that there will be someone in this Tribunal who could -- who could -- who could then translate the report to us into English. Unless he can have someone in Slovenia who could do that, with the approval of the Registrar. And since you know both English and Slovenian, perhaps you could take your time to check the two versions. And if -- I think that may be a better solution --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- if the registrar agrees as to the amount that needs to be paid. I mean, whether it's paid here or whether it's paid there, it has to be paid. So shall I leave this with you to discuss with your superiors? And then it's discussed, et cetera. If we can find -- if he can find someone -- maybe someone in his team is in a position to provide us with a translation or if you can do that yourself and ask to be compensated for further translating it into English, I think we can discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, I think it's risky for me to do that. I would be able to do it, certainly, but I really wouldn't like to mess with words. It wouldn't be a good idea, but it would be a very good idea if I could check the translation, it's not a problem, as to avoid mistakes because the translators sometimes don't know the right words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what we will do, Madam Registrar, is to communicate this problem to the Registrar, who's got now two weeks', three weeks' time to prepare for this. The report will need to be translated from Slovenian into English, and then we'll give the expert the opportunity to compare the two versions. And we will of course work on what we will have after that. All right. Okay. The documents that we will bring you -- that we will give you, all the ones that you will be signing for, will need to be returned. Now, if there will be an insistence on the part of the Registry to have them before the report, we will ask you to hand them before. Otherwise, you will bring them over with you when you come here with the original report or when you hand the original report to the Registrar, whichever is -- whichever is the case. I think it's going to be handing the original to the Registrar, I mean the original for translation purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, I think when somebody comes to pick up the report I can give the same person the materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, depending on how -- the time-frame that you create for yourself, you need to allow for a short time for the translation of these documents and also for coming over to give testimony. So I'm marking time. Roughly we're talking of any time from three to four weeks or, maximum, five weeks from now you will need to come over and give testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Well, I can -- I think I can assure you the expert opinion will be finished in the week from the 20th to 24th of February; that's when the opinion will be prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In that case, if we know a week beforehand that it's going to be ready that week, we will make arrangements for its connection --

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: You will know that next week. I will send the date when to be collected next week. There is no doubt about it. Thursday, Friday next week I will know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In that case, I told you before, we need original, plus five copies. It doesn't hold any further. We will need an original and one copy, an original and one copy in Slovenian, and then we will work on it for translation purposes. We will work on the copy for translation purposes. The Registrar needs to ensure that the translation is made within the shortest time possible, and I think we should aim at having a -- the gentleman come over and give testimony four weeks from now. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Brydensholt is making a very good point. You mentioned earlier that you would also be prepared to make a summary of the findings of the report in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, in that case we would require five copies of that because that would help us prepare better and also help the parties prepare better because they will know from the very word "go" where they stand as far as your expert report is concerned. All right? So let's try to recapitulate. You're going to examine these 11 documents by comparing them to the eight specimen signatures that I gave you earlier on. You're going to examine whether there was any tampering, and you're going to provide us also with any other information that you can dig-up that would help us in establishing authenticity or otherwise of the 11 documents. You're going to try to do this the shortest time possible, but you think you will require at least three weeks. You are going to file your report in Slovenian, two copies original and one copy. Together with it you will return all the documents that we have given you today. Accompanying your report there will be a summary of the report and findings in English, five copies. Then we will look in the rest. All right? I think I had another note somewhere, but I will find it. Is there anything else that -- yes, the note was exactly -- because I was informed that you wouldn't be able to come to testify in any case between the 13th and the 17th of this month, which is no longer -- no longer relevant. All right. So there will be two documents from [sic] you to sign. That one is undertaking -- basically I've prepared it that you will examine the documents entirely by non-destructive and non-damaging means to protect the physical integrity of the documents, ensure that they are returned as soon as the examination is completed to the Registry representative in a condition suitable for further examination, should it be required. And then I will also be handing to you for signature a receipt in which you confirm that you have received these documents, namely, the ones that are shown in the -- in this receipt and that the documents will be returned to Ms. Fabian as soon as the examination is completed. Do you wish Prosecution or Defence to see these two documents that we will require the witness -- the expert to sign?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, I don't think we need to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, usher, could you kindly please hand these documents. That's one here -- he needs to sign one of each because there are duplicates here. Dr. Kerzan, is there anything else you would like to tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I don't think so at this stage. I would just like to have a printout of this LiveNote which -- just to have it as a help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any problem with that? I mean, that's easy, we can procure. All right. So we will see you next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the sooner you can put us in the picture as to when to expect the result from you, the better it will be. And please always, in communicating with the Trial Chamber, you communicate via the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Registrar and not directly with us. The Registrar will give you the contact -- contact numbers, et cetera. If you are at any time approached by anyone in relation to the work -- usher. If you are at any time contacted from anyone, apart from the -- from my staff, please do let us know, report to us. I don't envisage happening, but it is my duty to caution you on this. And I think that brings to an end the meeting. I thank you so much for having come over, and we'll, please God, meet again when you have finished and prepared your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KERZAN
utterances.text: I think first week of March would probably be already to -- for me to come here and a week before I would have the document prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, parties, take note of that. There is a lot of work to be done in the meantime, so that doesn't really bother me at all at this time. And you have ample time as well in case you wish to have your experts present for the testimony of this witness. I would leave it at that for the time being, and we will pick it up again. You will expect communications from us by way of decisions next week, as I said, and we anxiously expect you to file -- both of you to file whatever you needed to file. One thing I forgot to -- in the -- last time -- yes, exactly. I forgot to give an exhibit number to the new P2 -- 328 and 329. You know exactly what I'm referring to. I said they will co-exist and proceed part and parcel with the existing ones. They will be 328.1 and 329.1. That's for your record because for our record we have already entered that. Thank you so much and have a good morning.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.34 a.m.
